items.title: CR: hosted lip-synced dialogue -- the first missing link is the dialogue door, not infinitetalk, and it is blocked on a Workflow binding the plane cannot emit
items.body:
**CR.** What blocks a HOSTED tenant from getting lip-synced dialogue, as a chain. Every number below
carries the command that produced it; every zero was given a positive control on the same matcher.
Measured 2026-09-27 against `vivijure-cf@8fc3f88` and `vivijure-control-plane@52a5a21`.

## The chain, and which link is first

Lip-synced dialogue needs three links, in this order:

| # | link | hosted today | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | a Cast with a voice | **present** | core-served, no module involved |
| 2 | a `dialogue` door to synthesize the line audio | **MISSING -- this is the first link** | both providers are unpublished AND unprovisionable |
| 3 | an audio-driven `motion.backend` door | **present in kind** | `alibaba-wan` is catalogued and IS audio-driven |

**Link 3 is not the gap, and that is the headline.** The framing this CR started from assumed
`infinitetalk` was the missing audio-driven door. It is not the only one. `alibaba-wan` declares
`driving_audio: true` (`vivijure-cf/modules/alibaba-wan/src/index.ts:73`) and genuinely consumes the
audio (`modules/alibaba-wan/src/wan.ts:38-39` maps `input.audio_url` onto `inputBody.audio`), and it
is row 6 of `TENANT_MODULE_CATALOG`. Core agrees there are two such doors of fifteen:
`film-orchestrator.js:722` says "13 of the 15 installed doors take this one" of the NON-driving leg.
So a hosted tenant already has an audio-driven mouth. What it has nothing to feed it.

### Link 1 is present, and that is its own defect

`GET /api/voices` -> `hListVoices` (`vivijure-cf/src/index.ts:291-294`, routed at `:2209`) returns
`catalogForDeploy(env, VOICE_CATALOG)`, and `VOICE_CATALOG` is a static const in the core package,
not a module projection. `catalogForDeploy` (`src/auth-gate.ts:186-188`) empties the list **only**
when `isDemoMode(env)`. A hosted tenant is token mode, so it is served the full TTS voice list, and
`hPatchCast` (`src/index.ts:305-321`) will validate and store a `voice_id` against it.

Nothing can then speak it. That is precisely the failure `catalogForDeploy` was written to prevent
for the demo deploy ("Serving the full list there advertises capability the deployment does not
have"), and the tenant case is not covered by it.

### Link 2 is missing twice over, and the second one is the hard one

Providers for the `dialogue` hook: `dialogue-gen` (`modules/dialogue-gen/src/index.ts:83`) and
`chatterbox` (`modules/chatterbox/src/index.ts:84`). Neither is in either tenant population:

- Population 3, PUBLISHED as a tenant bundle: `grep -v '^#' vivijure-cf/scripts/tenant-release-modules.txt | grep -c .` -> **22**, and neither name is in it (positive control `keyframe` -> present). That file is the single source `.github/workflows/studio-release.yml:242` resolves `TENANT_MODULES` from.
- Population 4, PROVISIONED, `TENANT_MODULE_CATALOG`: **17** (`npm run check:catalog` reads the live authority by array bounds and prints "17 entries"; the mirror agrees). Neither name is in it.

Publishing is a one-line edit. **The binding is not.** Both modules need a Workflows binding
(`modules/dialogue-gen/wrangler.toml` declares `DIALOGUE_WORKFLOW`, `modules/chatterbox/wrangler.toml`
declares `CHATTERBOX_WORKFLOW`), and this plane cannot emit one:

- `grep -c workflow src/tenant-modules.ts` -> **1**, and that one is the comment at `:214` flagging
  the gap ("Workflows (I2V_WORKFLOW) are still a FLAG if WfP cannot bind them"). Positive controls in
  the same 1858-line file: `ai` 223, `plain_text` 11, `secret_text` 7, `r2_bucket` 3, `d1` 2.
- The `WorkerBinding` union in `src/cf-api.ts:228-238` has ten variants and no workflow variant.
- The bundle cannot supply it either: `vivijure-cf/scripts/build-module-release.ts:73` writes a
  manifest of `{module, worker.sha256, compatibility_date, compatibility_flags}` and no bindings, so
  the array this plane builds at `src/tenant-modules.ts:680` IS the complete binding set a tenant
  module gets.

This is the same class as the `vpc_service` gap that keeps `audio-master`, `beat-sync`,
`film-titles` and `subtitle` published-but-uncatalogued: a catalog row without the binding is worse
than no row.

## What a hosted tenant actually experiences today

Three outcomes, and which one you get depends only on the door you pick. Two of the three are worse
than a refusal.

1. **A silent door** (`kling`, `minimax-hailuo`, `alibaba-wan-lora`, `cf-hh1-r2v`): refused at submit
   with a 400, `vivijure-cf/src/index.ts:982`, before any spend. This is the good case.
2. **A native-audio door** (`seedance`, `google-veo`, `vidu-q3`, `cf-seedance`, `cf-grok-video`,
   `cf-flux-3-video`): 201, the film completes, and core takes the declared degrade at
   `film-orchestrator.js:745`, `"no dialogue module installed; shipped a silent film"`. The door
   invents the speech from the prompt. The filmmaker picked a Cast voice and got a stranger's.
3. **`alibaba-wan`, the one audio-driven door they have**: 201, the entire keyframe pass is spent,
   and then `submitPreClipDialogue` hard-fails at `film-orchestrator.js:585` with
   `"no dialogue module bound"`. `wantsPreClipDialogue` (`:198-199`) routes a film there on exactly
   the `driving_audio` flag, so the better door is the one that fails latest and costs most.

The submit-time refusal text also names doors the tenant cannot have: `src/index.ts:983` says "Pick
a talking door (Seedance, InfiniteTalk, Wan, Veo, Flux, Vidu, or Grok)", and
`src/cast-voice-sample.ts:27-73` ships the same hardcoded promise to the voice picker. Neither list
is derived from the serving set. Filed separately as vivijure-cf#919.

## Fix class, per link

| link | fix class | whose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | none needed to enable; the advertise-without-capability defect is a projection fix | panel lane |
| 2a | publish `dialogue-gen` and/or `chatterbox` as tenant bundles (one line in `tenant-release-modules.txt` + a studio release) | wiring, mine |
| 2b | **teach the plane to bind a Workflow**: a `workflow` variant in `WorkerBinding` (`src/cf-api.ts:228-238`), the matching `bindings.push` in `uploadTenantModules`, and Workflow provisioning on the tenant account | engineering, mine, NOT wiring |
| 3 | optional: add `infinitetalk` as a second, better audio-driven door (see below) | wiring, mine, but MOOT until 2b lands |

## Adding `infinitetalk` -- three wiring points and one broken control

Worth doing after link 2, not before: it is the only door that REFUSES rather than inventing speech
(`modules/infinitetalk/src/index.ts:111`, `"infinitetalk: needs Cast audio (audio_url) so the
speaker stays ours"`, and `native_audio: false`), where `alibaba-wan` invents when the line is
missing. Its binding set is byte-shape-identical to `alibaba-wan`'s (`r2_buckets R2_RENDERS`,
`secrets_store_secrets RUNPOD_API_KEY`, `d1_databases TELEMETRY_DB`), so it asks the plane for
nothing new.

1. `vivijure-cf/scripts/tenant-release-modules.txt` + a studio release, then `STUDIO_RELEASE`
   advanced on the plane. **Ordering matters and typecheck will not catch it**: a catalog row that
   names a module the pinned release does not publish fails EVERY provision at `modules_upload`.
2. A `TENANT_MODULE_CATALOG` row, shaped like the eight cost-door rows:
   `{ module: "infinitetalk", publicEndpoint: "infinitetalk", recordsRunpodJobs: true, writesTenantRenders: true }`.
3. `PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST` in `src/runpod-proxy.ts:55-64` (8 entries today, `infinitetalk` not
   among them). `isAllowedEndpoint` (`:227-231`) refuses any slug in neither the tenant pool nor that
   list, so without this the proxy rejects every submit. This is a generic meter-integrity
   allowlist, not an anti-infinitetalk gate.

**And one control breaks.** `tests/shared-pool-key-scope.live.test.ts:20` uses
`const OUT_OF_SCOPE_CONTROL = "infinitetalk"` as the NEGATIVE control proving the shared invoke key
cannot reach an endpoint it should not (`:55-65`). Bringing infinitetalk into scope silently turns
that assertion into a tautology. Replace the control in the same PR, or the suite keeps passing
while losing the only reading that proves its instrument can fail.

## Unwired or deliberately withheld?

**Unwired, everywhere. Nothing withholds any of these four modules.**
`grep -rc` in `vivijure-control-plane/src/`: `infinitetalk` **6**, `chatterbox` **0**,
`dialogue-gen` **0**, `cast-image` **0**; positive controls `keyframe` **29**, `seedance` **3**. All
six `infinitetalk` hits are comments (`src/runpod.ts:151,160`, `src/satellite-pins.ts:57,64`,
`src/tenant-modules.ts:167,173`). A sweep of `vivijure-cf/src` for a self-host-only flag, denylist or
hosted-tier gate keyed on a module returns nothing.

## The one decision that is Conrad's

Stated once, and it is already open as cp#190, so this CR adds no second issue for it:
**whether a hosted tenant's per-call dialogue and lip-sync spend is billed to the tenant or absorbed
by us.** Everything above is engineering; that is not.

Supporting numbers, confirmed independently so the decision is not taken on a remembered figure:
`infinitetalk` is a RunPod PUBLIC endpoint (`list-public-endpoints`: owner MeiGen-AI, `isLive` true,
`baseUrl https://api.runpod.ai/v2/infinitetalk`, pricing `"480p: $0.25"`), not one of ours
(`list-endpoints` on our account returns exactly 2: `vivijure-backend` max 40 workers and
`vivijure-wan-train` max 10, which is also where the 50-slot figure comes from). So it holds zero of
our 50 slots and costs nothing at rest; it bills per call. `chatterbox-turbo` is likewise a public
endpoint, and `dialogue-gen` bills through our AI Gateway on unified billing
(`@cf/deepgram/aura-1`), which is our credit either way.

## Landed alongside this CR

- vivijure-cf#920 -- ten module `wrangler.toml` files asserted "TENANT_MODULE_CATALOG is six
  entries, none of them these" (it is 17 and eight of them ARE these), and warned of a cross-tenant
  TELEMETRY_DB write that the plane already prevents by binding `R2_RENDERS` to `tenantBucketName`
  and `TELEMETRY_DB` to `telemetryD1Id`, throwing in both cases. Also `modules/infinitetalk`
  described itself as a Kling worker in two files.
- vivijure#827 -- `docs/CAPABILITIES.md` footnote `[^talk]`.

## Not fixed, noted

`modules/kling-o1-r2v/wrangler.toml:1` and `src/index.ts:1` call it "Kuaishou Kling V2.1 I2V Pro".
Right vendor, wrong model: it is Kling Video O1 R2V. Left alone to keep the PR to its subject.

items.title: video-finish normalizes every clip to a FIXED 1920x1080 regardless of what the door produced: 12 of 15 installed motion doors are upscaled today, and the sizing contract quotes a reject guard as a payload
items.body:
Raised while sizing the `partialUrls` pool (vivijure-core#301). **Two separate findings.** The first is a structural defect with a product decision attached; the second is a correctness problem in a number that was about to become a contract.

> **REVISED 2026-09-27.** An earlier draft treated `alibaba-wan` as "the i2v renderer" and recommended defaulting the route to 1280x720. **That was wrong and is withdrawn.** `motion.backend` fans out to **15 INSTALLED doors** (corrected 2026-09-27, see the census denominator below: 17 is the buildable count, not the installed one), most of which take resolution as caller input, so a 720p default would DOWNSCALE any job that asked for more. The finding is restated structurally below, which is the form that survives whichever renderer is picked. Renderer ranking is parked in vivijure#826 and this does not wait on it.

---

# FINDING 1: normalization targets a FIXED 1920x1080 regardless of what the door produced

## The defect

`containers/video-finish` scales and pads every clip to a target chosen by `resolveDeliveryResolution(job)`. That function reads **exactly two fields and nothing else**:

```ts
// vivijure-core/src/film-model.ts:1482-1489
export function resolveDeliveryResolution(
  job: { delivery_width?: unknown; delivery_height?: unknown },
): DeliveryResolution {
  const w = positiveInt(job?.delivery_width);
  const h = positiveInt(job?.delivery_height);
  if (w && h) return { width: w, height: h, decided: true };
  return { width: DEFAULT_DELIVERY_WIDTH, height: DEFAULT_DELIVERY_HEIGHT, decided: false };
}
```

**Nothing about the source clip feeds into it**, and **nothing in either repo ever sets `delivery_width` / `delivery_height` on a job.** Verified: every occurrence in `src/` is a read, a type declaration or a pass-through; the only writes are in tests. The code says so itself at `film-model.ts:217` -- *"Absent today on every job."*

**So in production the target is always 1920x1080**, and `containers/video-finish/app.py:593-596` applies it unconditionally, with no source-equals-target short circuit:

```python
vf = (
    f"scale={width}:{height}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"
    f"pad={width}:{height}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,fps={fps}"
)
```

Every clip is then re-encoded through `libx264 -crf 18 -preset medium` (`app.py:612`) whether or not it needed anything.

**The route cannot distinguish "this needs no work" from "this needs a 1.95x upscale that adds no detail" from "this would be a destructive downscale."** That is the defect.

## Why the obvious fix is also wrong

The natural place to put a fix is a per-door lookup table of native resolutions. **That cannot work: 8 of the 15 doors take resolution as CALLER INPUT, so the same door produces different resolutions on different jobs.** There is no per-door constant to keep correct. A fixed target is wrong **by construction**, not merely mistuned.

## The rule

Two halves, symmetric, and the second is the one an over-eager fix would break:

- **Never upscale.** If the door produced 720p, finish at 720p. Interpolated pixels cost bytes and CPU and carry no information that was not there.
- **Never downscale.** If the door produced 1080p or 4k, do not destroy it to hit a constant.

**The target should MATCH THE SOURCE, with an explicit operator override** (`delivery_width`/`delivery_height`, which already exist and are already plumbed -- they are simply never set).

## This is one hop from done, because the measurement already exists

**No new probe, no container change, no D1 migration.** The source resolution is already measured, already persisted, and already on the wire to a different consumer:

1. **Measured** in the Worker with bounded R2 range reads of the mp4 `tkhd` box -- no ffprobe, no container round trip (`vivijure-core/src/clip-validate.ts:157-169`), on every done clip from every door via the single chokepoint `validateDoneClips` (`render-orchestrator.ts:663-666`).
2. **Persisted** onto the clip record (`render-orchestrator.ts:674-675`, fields at `clip-job-model.ts:39-41`):
   ```ts
   if (typeof res.checks?.width === "number" && res.checks.width > 0) shot.delivered_width = res.checks.width;
   ```
3. **Read back** by `measuredClipDimensions(env, job)` (`film-orchestrator.ts:1155-1177`).
4. **Already handed to `finish` modules** so `finish-upscale` can avoid undershooting (`film-orchestrator.ts:1225-1232`).

**`measuredClipDimensions` has exactly ONE caller: `film-orchestrator.ts:1183`, the finish chain.** The **assemble** path at `film-orchestrator.ts:2485` calls `resolveDeliveryResolution(job)` and never looks at it, so `video-finish` is handed 1920x1080 with no idea what it is normalizing. **The numbers are sitting at the assemble seam already and are simply not read there.**

## The per-door census

> **This table is a census of what the CODE AND DOCS CLAIM. It is NOT a measurement of output.** No row is marked observed: this seat has zero real rendered clips and no R2 credentials, so nothing here was checked against a real artifact. Evidence class is `DECLARED` (module code says so), `DOCUMENTED` (only prose or an endpoint name says so), or `UNMEASURED`.

**CORRECTED DENOMINATOR, 2026-09-27: 15, not 17.** The earlier figure came from the `modules/`
directory listing, which is the wrong instrument: a module directory is a **buildable worker**, not
an **installed door**. Measured three ways, and the three disagree for one reason:

| instrument | count | command |
|---|---|---|
| `modules/` directories | 35 (34 real; `_shared/` is 8 helper `.ts` files with no manifest) | `ls -d modules/*/ \| wc -l` |
| manifests declaring `hooks: ["motion.backend"]` | **17** | `grep -rl motion.backend modules/*/src/{index,manifest}.ts`, filtered on the `hooks:` line |
| **the LIVE projection** `hooks["motion.backend"]` | **15** | `GET /api/modules` on the deployed `vivijure-studio` (`studio_release: 1.34.0`, `host.dispatch: true`) |

**Reconciliation, and there is no third discrepancy.** The projection is built by `discoverModules`
inside `hModules` (`src/index.ts:2164-2167`), which enumerates `MODULE_*` service bindings on the
deployed worker plus enabled `installed_modules` D1 rows. A directory with neither is invisible to
it, correctly. Exactly two doors are in the manifest count and absent from the projection, and both
absences are deliberate and documented in-repo:

| door | why it is not installed |
|---|---|
| `kling` | `wrangler.toml.example:321`: *"Kling 2.1 stays in modules/kling but is NOT bound on hosted."* Binding commented out at `:322-324`. |
| `local-gpu` | `wrangler.toml.example:312`: *"HOSTED NEVER BINDS THIS. Conrad: local-gpu belongs on vivijure-local only."* |

17 - 2 = 15. Both were `UNDETERMINED` rows, so **removing them does not change the 12 upscaled; it
only shrinks the denominator**, which makes the finding stronger rather than weaker: 12 of 15, not
12 of 17.

**Where "14" comes from, recorded so it is not re-derived:** counting the `MODULE_*` bindings by eye
misses `MODULE_INFINITETALK` (`wrangler.toml.example:331`), which sits mid-block between
`MODULE_KLING_O1_R2V` and `MODULE_CHATTERBOX` rather than with the other cloud doors. A scripted
count returns 15.

Of the 18 non-motion module directories: audio, keyframe/stills, subtitle, notify, plan, and the
`finish` post-processors, which transform an existing clip rather than producing one.
**3 of the 15 doors are fully UNMEASURED, 1 partial.**

| Door | Declared resolution | Evidence | Caller-settable? | vs the 1920x1080 target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alibaba-wan` (**Wan 2.6**, not 2.2) | `"720p"` hardcoded (`src/wan.ts:30`); no `resolution` knob in `config_schema`, confirmed against the live projection | DECLARED | **No** | **UPSCALE** |
| `alibaba-wan-lora` | prose + endpoint name only (`index.ts:2,60`) | DOCUMENTED | No | UPSCALE if prose is right, unverified |
| `cf-flux-3-video` | enum `hd`/`fhd`, default `hd` (`index.ts:82`); **no pixel dims anywhere** | DECLARED (token) / UNMEASURED (pixels) | Yes | probably UPSCALE, cannot confirm |
| `cf-grok-video` | enum `480p`/`720p`, default `720p` (`index.ts:93`) | DECLARED | Yes | **UPSCALE** at both |
| `cf-hailuo` | enum `768P`/`1080P`, default `768P` (`index.ts:82`) | DECLARED | Yes | UPSCALE at default, passthrough at `1080P` |
| `cf-hh1-r2v` | enum `720P`/`1080P`, default `720P` (`index.ts:82`) | DECLARED | Yes | UPSCALE at default, passthrough at `1080P` |
| `cf-seedance` | enum `480p`/`720p`/`1080p`/`4k`, default `720p` (`index.ts:88`) | DECLARED | Yes | UPSCALE at default, passthrough at `1080p`, **DOWNSCALE at `4k`** |
| `cf-veo` | enum `720p`/`1080p`, **default `720p`** (`index.ts:84`) | DECLARED | Yes | UPSCALE at default, passthrough at `1080p` |
| `google-veo` | `"720p"` hardcoded (`src/veo.ts:31`) | DECLARED | **No** | **UPSCALE** |
| `infinitetalk` | enum `480p`/`720p`, default `480p` (`index.ts:45`) | DECLARED | Yes | **UPSCALE 2.25x linear** at default |
| `seedance` | `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = "720p"` (`src/seedance.ts:18,34`) | DECLARED | Yes | **UPSCALE** at both |
| `vidu-q3` | `size: "720p"` hardcoded (`src/vidu.ts:26`) | DECLARED | **No** | **UPSCALE** |
| `kling-o1-r2v` | none sent | **UNMEASURED** | No | UNDETERMINED |
| `minimax-hailuo` | none sent | **UNMEASURED** | No | UNDETERMINED |
| `own-gpu` | none in this repo; set by backend `quality` tier | **UNMEASURED** | indirect | UNDETERMINED |

**At default config, every INSTALLED door whose resolution is knowable from the repo is
UPSCALED. Zero pass through.** Out of **15**: 12 upscale, 3 undetermined (`kling-o1-r2v`,
`minimax-hailuo`, `own-gpu`), 0 passthrough, 0 downscale. Four doors *can* be configured to pass
through and one (`cf-seedance`) can be configured to be DOWNSCALED, at `4k`. **Not one installed
door is a verified fixed-native-1080p producer.**

> The two doors dropped from this table versus the earlier 17-row version are `kling` and
> `local-gpu`, neither of which is bound on hosted. They are excluded from the denominator, not
> deleted from the record: see the reconciliation above. Both were UNDETERMINED, so the 12 is
> unchanged.

**The waste is therefore broad and it is being paid today**, not after a renderer re-evaluation. It is not confined to one door: `cf-veo`, `cf-seedance`, `cf-hailuo`, `cf-hh1-r2v`, `cf-grok-video`, `seedance` and `infinitetalk` all **default** below the target.

Note the four hardcoded values (`alibaba-wan`, `google-veo`, `vidu-q3`, and `alibaba-wan-lora` by omission) are **our choices frozen in our code, not provider ceilings.**

## Census method, and a second correction to it

**TWO installed doors declare audio-driven motion, not one: `infinitetalk` AND `alibaba-wan`.**
Measured across every module directory, negatives included:

```
$ grep -rn "driving_audio: true" modules/
modules/infinitetalk/src/index.ts:64:    driving_audio: true,
modules/alibaba-wan/src/index.ts:73:    driving_audio: true,
```

**The method matters more than the count.** The declared capability lives in the manifest's `usage`
block, not in the request field, so grepping module source for `audio_url` finds the
IMPLEMENTATION and misses the CONTRACT. That grep returns **8** module directories
(`alibaba-wan audio-master beat-sync chatterbox finish-blender finish-rife finish-upscale
infinitetalk`), six of which are not `motion.backend` doors at all. Every row in the census above
is read from the declared manifest for the same reason.

Not to be folded in: `cf-seedance` declares `voice_ref: true`, which is a Cast sample used as a
reference video. That is a different mechanism from audio-driven motion and does not belong in this
count.

**`alibaba-wan` is Wan 2.6.** `ENDPOINT_ID = "wan-2-6-i2v"` (`src/index.ts:42`), `provides` label
*"Talking (Wan 2.6)"* (`:50`), and zero occurrences of `2.2` anywhere under `modules/alibaba-wan/`.
The "2.2" belongs to its siblings and was mis-attributed: `grep -rln 'Wan 2\.2\|Wan2\.2'` hits
`modules/alibaba-wan-lora/` and `modules/own-gpu/` (plus `wrangler.toml.example:306`), which is the
positive control showing that zero is a real zero and not a broken pattern.

## Second axis of the same defect: aspect ratio

`pad=` letterboxes or pillarboxes anything that is not 16:9 into a 1920x1080 landscape frame. `cf-hh1-r2v` offers `9:16`, `3:4`, `21:9`, `5:4`, `9:21` (`index.ts:83`); `cf-seedance` and `cf-grok-video` are similar. **A `9:16` vertical clip currently ships as a pillarboxed strip inside a landscape film.** Same fixed-target root cause, different axis, and a fix that only addresses resolution leaves it in place.

## What is Conrad's

**The rule above is engineering and does not need him.** What does: **is 1080p delivery a tier we offer and charge for, independent of what the door produced?**

The census is the input to that. 8 doors expose resolution to the caller, so "the operator can choose 1080p and pay the encode" is available on those. On `alibaba-wan`, `google-veo` and `vidu-q3` it is not -- those will only ever hand back 720p as currently coded, so a 1080p deliverable there means an explicit upscale someone is choosing to buy, not a better render.

---

# FINDING 2: the sizing contract quotes a reject guard as a payload

## Both halves of the proposed contract are wrong

The proposal was **8 GB total source bytes as 32 x 256 MB**, resting on the assumption that **normalized bytes track source bytes**.

**a. 256 MB is a reject ceiling, not a payload.** `MAX_CLIP_BYTES` (`app.py:40`) is the argument to `_download(s, url, dst, MAX_CLIP_BYTES)` at `app.py:285` and `:416` -- the size at which a download is REFUSED. The repo already reads it as a payload in three more places, so it is a habit and not a slip: `README.md:69`, `CHANGELOG.md:12` and `app.py:184` all present `MAX_CLIPS 80 x MAX_CLIP_BYTES 256 MB = 20.0 GB` as an expected disk figure.

At the container's settings a 256 MB clip is **3.2 to 15.6 minutes** of video. Clips are **4 to 8 seconds** (`clipSeconds` default 8.0, `docs/CONTRACT.md:1014`). So 256 MB is **24x to 58x** above what a clip can weigh.

Measured: **32 clips x 8 s normalizes to roughly 70-350 MB** against a contract saying 8 GB, i.e. **23x to 120x high**. A full 80-clip film is about **750 MB**. Nothing approaches the 20 GB ephemeral disk.

**b. Normalized bytes do NOT track source bytes.** Measured ratio spans **0.98x to 5.09x**, dominated by whatever bitrate the source happened to carry. The stable component is FINDING 1's upscale: **~1.95x** for a 720p source pushed to 1080p.

## Knock-on: the peak-disk budget uses the wrong multiplier

`app.py:49-50` budgets peak as `3 x (MAX_BATCH_BYTES + MAX_CLIP_BYTES)` -- sources, normalized copies, partial. **That assumes normalized is about equal to source.** With the upscale in play normalized is about 2x source, so the right multiplier against SOURCE bytes is **~5x, not 3x**. It does not bite today only because absolute sizes sit two orders of magnitude below the guards, and fixing FINDING 1 removes the inflation rather than re-tuning the constant.

## What the contract should say

Bytes per second at the configured CRF, times duration, times count:

| target | measured normalized bitrate | realistic band |
|---|---|---|
| 1080p24 crf 18 medium | 0.40 - 11.16 Mbps | ~2.3 - 9.3 Mbps |
| 720p24 crf 18 medium | 0.17 - 4.82 Mbps | ~0.9 - 4.8 Mbps |

Keep 256 MB as the per-clip reject ceiling, which is what it is.

---

## Measurement provenance

**PROXIES, not real output. Denominator: 8 clips measured, ZERO real rendered clips, ZERO R2 objects listed.** This seat holds no R2 credentials (`AWS_*`, `R2_*`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` unset; no `~/.aws`, no rclone config), so no real clip was reachable to measure or even to size from metadata.

Proxies were slow pans over a real photographic still at 8.0 s / 16 fps, in four complexity brackets, encoded then normalized through the container's exact command.

**Direction of error.** Pan brackets **underestimate**: no subject deformation, no generated per-frame shimmer, near-global motion vectors. Injected-noise brackets **overestimate**: IID noise compresses worse than structured diffusion shimmer. Real generated video at 1080p24 crf 18 most likely lands in the upper half of the 2-9 Mbps band, but that is inference.

**The verdicts do not depend on proxy precision.** Making 256 MB reachable at 8 s needs about **256 Mbps**; the worst bracket reached **11 Mbps**. Conclusion survives a 20x proxy error.

**The ~1.95x is the most robust figure here**, because it is a ratio between two encodes of the SAME source and cancels most of the proxy's character. Trust that one; discount the absolute byte counts.

## Acceptance

- **FINDING 1 rule implemented at the assemble seam**: target matches measured source per film, `delivery_*` as explicit override. Reads `measuredClipDimensions`, which already exists.
- **Demonstrated both ways**: a 720p-source film assembles at 720p (no upscale), and a 1080p-source film is NOT downscaled. A rule proven in one direction only is half a rule.
- A film of MIXED source resolutions has a defined, documented outcome. The current code has one by accident; it should have one by choice.
- Aspect ratio addressed or explicitly deferred with a reason, since `pad=` is the same root cause.
- Conrad rules on 1080p as a priced deliverable tier.
- Capacity contract restated as bitrate x duration x count, with the proxy caveat carried.
- `app.py:49-50`, `README.md:69`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`, `app.py:184` corrected.
- The 5 UNMEASURED doors resolved when a real clip from each is reachable.

Refs #784, #801, vivijure-core#301, vivijure#826

### What happened?

The managed runtime release triggered by CLI `v0.26.1` failed before publication in [run 40108617281](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40108617281).

The [release job](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40108617281/job/120924941572) succeeded through building the matching CLI prerequisites, verifying/installing the SDK from the same source, setting the server artifact version, verifying the executable JAR/publication profile, and retaining the verified JAR/checksum. It then failed in **Recheck the immutable tag and existing publication bytes**.

Every subsequent publication step was skipped: Central signing setup, Central publication, Central availability verification, GitHub asset attachment, OSS uploader setup, OSS upload and public-download verification. This run did not execute those publication steps. Whether matching artifacts already exist through another publication path has not been established.

At the time of the audit, this was still the newest managed-runtime workflow run. The preceding nightly runs [40034332964](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40034332964) and [39865408215](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/39865408215) also failed, but their causes have not been compared.

### What did you expect to happen?

A stable CLI release should produce the matching managed runtime distribution after verification. If the immutable-publication guard refuses publication, its diagnostic should identify which tag or publication URL failed and distinguish an existing-byte mismatch from an inaccessible endpoint, so the release can be recovered without overwriting immutable artifacts.

### Client information

This is a GitHub Actions release failure:

- CLI/managed runtime version: `0.26.1`
- Run commit: `b475278c4a300acebe6cfc990a9e1b1d18819bfc`
- Workflow: `Release Managed server runtime`
- Job: `release`, GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`
- Toolchains configured by the workflow: Java 21 and Node.js 22
- Failed step: `Recheck the immutable tag and existing publication bytes`

### Anything else we need to know?

The exact terminal error in the complete job log is:

```text
2026-10-24T17:33:20.1959977Z true
2026-10-24T17:33:21.9187526Z Cannot verify existing release artifact: HTTP 403.
2026-10-24T17:33:21.9268240Z ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The `true` is the result of the published-release check after the tag comparison, so execution passed the tag check and failed while verifying an artifact URL. The step checks Central, GitHub and OSS in sequence, but the error does not include the URL; the log alone cannot identify which endpoint returned 403. This is not evidence of a byte mismatch.

The verified JAR and checksum were retained in [artifact 12569715300](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40108617281/artifacts/12569715300), named `managed-runtime-0.26.1`.

The next diagnostic step is to identify which artifact URL returned 403 and distinguish an absent artifact from inaccessible publication state before choosing a recovery. No retry, artifact replacement or credential change was performed during the audit.

[#15465](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/15465) tracks postrelease runner queueing/migration; this report tracks the separate publication failure after the job started. A bounded search for managed-runtime release failures and the immutable-tag check did not identify an exact existing report.

items.title: [BUG] outputKind classifies 109 image/audio/video generators as text because their output also lists text
items.body:
## What it is

`outputKind` special-cases `embedding` and `score`, then falls through to "does the output list include text". A model whose output is `["audio","text"]` or `["image","text"]` therefore classifies as **`text`** — a chat model — when the non-text element is what it actually produces.

`keysync/keysync.mjs`:

```js
export function outputKind(entry) {
  const out = entry?.modalities?.output;
  if (!Array.isArray(out) || out.length === 0) return null;
  if (out.includes("embedding") || out.includes("score")) return "nontext";
  return out.includes("text") ? "text" : "nontext";
}
```

The two-name allowlist was derived from the embedding case (OQ-3, `nvidia/bge-m3`) and never widened to the other generative modalities.

## Evidence

```
lyria                  output = ["audio"]          outputKind = nontext   correct
lyria-3-pro-preview    output = ["audio","text"]   outputKind = text      WRONG
veo-2                  output = ["video"]          outputKind = nontext   correct
```

Measured across all 4,298 bundle entries — those whose output contains `text` plus at least one other modality:

| shape | count |
|---|--:|
| `text` + `audio` | 54 |
| `text` + `image` | 43 |
| `text` + `embedding` | 16 |
| `text` + `video` | 10 |
| `text` + `score` | 2 |
| `text` + `audio` + `image` | 2 |
| **total** | **127** |
| caught by the current `embedding`/`score` clause | 18 |
| **misclassified as `text`** | **109** |

## Impact

`outputKind` gates three things, and all three are wrong for these 109:

1. **Selectability.** `menu/style.mjs` dims and the row selector skips on `outputKind === "nontext"`. A music or image generator renders as an ordinary selectable chat model.
2. **Declaration.** Non-text rows are excluded from `behavesAs` bucketing; these are not, so an image generator receives a chat model's client-side capability profile.
3. **The `ctx` cell.** Renders a context number rather than the non-chat marker.

`lyria` (bare) is caught because its output is `["audio"]` alone; `lyria-3-pro-preview` is not. So the same model family splits across both classifications on a field the provider populated inconsistently.

## Fix

Invert the rule rather than extending the allowlist. A model's **output** modalities describe what it emits; if any of them is not text, the non-text element is the product and any accompanying text is incidental — a caption, a transcript, a description.

```js
return out.every((m) => m === "text") ? "text" : "nontext";
```

That subsumes the `embedding`/`score` clause and needs no per-modality list, so a future upstream modality name cannot silently fall through the way `audio` did.

**Input modalities are unaffected and must stay unaffected** — a vision model that accepts images and answers in prose has `output: ["text"]` and remains correctly classified as text. This changes only what a model *produces*.

## Why the current shape was reasonable and still wrong

The positive-signal-only reasoning in `plans/model-capability-buckets-plan.md` §1.5 is sound: `modalities.output` is present on 100% of entries, so `["text"]` is likely a default rather than an assertion, and only a positive **non-text** signal should block a row. This fix follows that rule exactly — `["audio","text"]` carries a positive non-text signal and should block. The defect is that the implementation treated "positive non-text signal" as a two-name list instead of as the complement of text.

## Interaction with in-flight work

Two dependencies, both current:

- **A revision in flight adds `outputKind` as a sort term ahead of free-first** in `buildProviders`'s ranking, to stop a repaired `inferTier` promoting free rerank and embedding models into the native picker. Measured effect of that term: non-text rows in the summed top-3 fall from 56 to 23. With this bug fixed, the term reaches the remaining cases — `google` currently keeps `lyria-3-pro-preview` and `lyria-3-clip-preview` in its top 3 purely because of this misclassification.
- **The live listing's `capability` field** (`chat|audio|image_gen|embedding|vision|rerank|moderation`) is the intended fresher override for `outputKind`. That closes the same class from a different direction and is a separate task; this fix is independent of it and should not wait for it, since the bundle remains the source for every provider whose listing lacks the field.

## Related

- OQ-3 — `nvidia/bge-m3` declared `output: ["text"]`, the case that produced the original two-name clause. Different shape: that one has no positive non-text signal at all and this fix does not address it.
- #43 — no per-model modality is carried; `outputKind` collapses `["image"]`, `["audio"]`, `["video"]` to one string. This fix corrects *which* rows are non-text without changing that they are all labelled identically.

items.title: 17 of 40 Cloud IaaS records are not infrastructure, and 11 are named with a bare generic noun

labels.name: parked
labels.description: Not on the work order (#1131). Do not pick up unless the work order lists it.

items.body:
## What a reader sees

`/vendor/cloudways`, live now, under the heading **Cloudways Free Tier 2026**:

> **Free Tier Details** — 30% off for 3 months.
>
> **When You'll Outgrow Cloudways's Free Tier** — When your usage exceeds the free tier limits,
> you'll need to upgrade. At that point, **consider Connect** which offers Free in the same category.
>
> **Alternatives in Cloud IaaS** — Connect, Oracle Cloud, Projects, filebase.com, Notebook,
> Google Colab, Wiki, Checkout, Zoho Assist, Desk, Meeting, Cliq

Nine of those twelve are Zoho SaaS apps. We tell a reader who outgrows managed cloud hosting to
consider **Zoho Connect**, a team intranet. `Notebook`'s own description in our index is *"A free
alternative to Evernote."*

## The cause is the category, not the alternatives engine

`Cloud IaaS` holds 40 records. **17 are not infrastructure:**

- **13 Zoho products** — `Zoho`, `Zoho Assist`, `Docs`, `Projects`, `Connect`, `Meeting`, `Vault`,
  `Showtime`, `Notebook`, `Wiki`, `Checkout`, `Desk`, `Cliq`. Password manager, help desk, team
  chat, wiki, billing pages, webinars.
- **3 object stores** — `4EVERLAND`, `C2 Object Storage`, `filebase.com`. `Storage` exists and has
  52 records.
- **`Google Colab`** — hosted Jupyter notebooks.

`/category/cloud-iaas` renders all 40 and every page in the category prints *"One of 40 Cloud IaaS
services we track"*. This is upstream of https://github.com/robhunter/agentdeals/issues/1032: that
issue is about alternatives that share a category and are not substitutes. Here the category itself
is not a category, so same-category membership carries no information at all.

## 11 records are named with a bare generic noun

`Docs`, `Projects`, `Connect`, `Meeting`, `Vault`, `Showtime`, `Notebook`, `Wiki`, `Checkout`,
`Desk`, `Cliq`. Each has `url: zoho.com/<slug>`, so the vendor is recoverable from the record — the
`vendor` field simply drops it.

Two consequences beyond the reader:

- **`Vault` collides with HashiCorp Vault**, and `Docs`, `Projects`, `Connect`, `Checkout`, `Desk`
  are words that appear as subjects in editorial prose across the site.
- The alias map in https://github.com/robhunter/agentdeals/issues/1073 AC-2 cannot repair these.
  An alias maps a variant spelling to a vendor; here there is no variant, the stored name is a
  common noun. They will resolve to *something* and it will be wrong.

## `30% off for 3 months` is not a free tier

The Cloudways record is `tier: "Startup Program"` and renders under `Free Tier 2026` with
`stability: stable` and *"zero pricing changes recorded. This is a good sign — stable pricing."*
Zero changes recorded because the URL we read does not mention Cloudways —
https://github.com/robhunter/agentdeals/issues/1109. A percentage discount and a free tier are
different products and the page conflates them in its title, its badge and its prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The 17 non-infrastructure records leave `Cloud IaaS`. The 3 object stores go to `Storage`. Say
   where each of the other 14 lands; do not create a category to hold one record.
2. **Every record's `vendor` names the vendor.** The 11 bare nouns become their real product names.
   Report any other record in the index whose `vendor` does not appear in its own `url` host or
   description — I have only audited the Zoho block.
3. A test fails the build when a record's `vendor` is a single common noun that matches no host in
   its own `url`. The Zoho 11 are the seed.
4. **`tier` values that describe a discount do not render under a "Free Tier" heading.** Report how
   many records carry a percentage discount or a credit as their free-tier description; the Cloudways
   row is one and the 85 on #1109 are likely most of the rest.
5. The alternatives shown on a vendor page are drawn from the corrected categories, and
   `/vendor/cloudways` no longer offers a team intranet as a substitute for managed hosting.
6. Category counts rendered on pages (`One of 40 Cloud IaaS services we track`, `40 offers`) are
   recomputed, not hardcoded.

## Priority

`priority/high`. It is live, it is on a content page, and it is the kind of error a reader can spot
without checking anything — which is the sort that costs us the trust the rest of this work is
buying.

/label priority/high
/label type: bug

items.title: The `no-licence-url` abstention conflates two populations: its prose says `asserts an spdxId` but six records assert neither field, and a test pins the conflation
items.body:
Found by the independent QA gate on #1057 as a non-blocking observation, and independently reproduced here against trunk `1a86cf9e` on `2026-09-06T23:27Z`. It shipped with #1057 and affects no verdict, no dataset value and no exit code — the derived coverage table is correct. It is a **reporting** defect, and it is the same class of defect #1057 was filed about, reproduced inside the fix for it.

### Outcome

`no-licence-url` is returned for two different populations, and its prose describes only one of them. A reader of the abstention report is told that every record in the bucket asserts an `spdxId`. Six of them assert nothing at all.

### The two return sites

`web/src/lib/licence-url-identity.ts`:

```ts
320:  if (spdxId === undefined || spdxId.length === 0) {
321:    return abstain(recordedUrl === undefined || recordedUrl.length === 0 ? 'no-licence-url' : 'no-spdx-id');
322:  }
323:  if (recordedUrl === undefined || recordedUrl.length === 0) return abstain('no-licence-url');
```

- **Line 323** — `spdxId` present, URL absent. This is the documented population.
- **Line 321** — **neither** field present. Also `no-licence-url`, and the prose is false for it.

The prose, at line 515, and the identical doc comment at line 93:

```ts
'no-licence-url': 'asserts an `spdxId` but cites no URL, so the sweep never sees this record at all',
```

The second clause is true of both populations. The first clause is true of only one.

### Measurement

Partitioning `web/src/data/releases.json` at trunk by the two fields:

| population | count | routed to | prose accurate? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spdxId` and `url` | 28 | (checked) | — |
| `spdxId`, no `url` | **14** | `no-licence-url` | yes |
| `url`, no `spdxId` | 29 | `no-spdx-id` | yes |
| **neither** | **6** | **`no-licence-url`** | **no** |
| no `license` object | 46 | — | — |

Control: the partition sums to 123/123, so nothing is being double-counted or dropped.

**This is the self-contradiction in one document.** The bucket is reported as **20** (14 + 6) while the prose describes **14**. Both numbers are correct about different things and neither says which.

The six records asserting neither field:

```
alibaba-qwen3-8-2-4t-a95b
kyutai-moshiko-pytorch-bf16
lelapa-ai-inkubalm-0-4b
maritaca-ai-sabia-7b
nvidia-nemotron-nano-9b-v2
tencent-hunyuanimage-3-0-standard
```

### The test suite cannot catch it — it pins it

`web/src/lib/licence-url-identity.test.ts:219`:

```ts
it('names a missing URL for the population the sweep never sees', () => {
  expect(classifyLicenceIdentity({ spdxId: 'Apache-2.0' }).reason).toBe('no-licence-url');
  expect(classifyLicenceIdentity({}).reason).toBe('no-licence-url');   // <- the neither-field case
});
```

The second assertion is exactly the conflated input, and it asserts the current behaviour is correct. So this is not a gap in coverage that a new test closes quietly — **the existing test encodes the conflation**, and any fix must change it. Worth knowing before someone starts.

The relation that would have failed — bucket size ≠ prose population, `20 ≠ 14` — is never asserted anywhere.

### Why this is worth fixing despite being non-blocking

#1057 was filed because *a sweep measured reachability and read as correctness* — an instrument whose output invited a conclusion its measurement did not support. This is that shape again, one layer in: a bucket measures "has no URL" and its label reads as "asserts an spdxId but has no URL". A reader who acts on the label will look for an SPDX identifier on six records that have none.

### Suggested direction, not a prescription

Splitting the reason enum is the obvious move — `no-licence-url` for line 323 and something like `no-licence-fields` for line 321 — which makes the two populations separately countable and lets the prose be true of each. The alternative, widening the prose to cover both, keeps one bucket but gives up the ability to report the populations separately, and the 14/20 ambiguity is exactly what makes that undesirable.

Either way the change is confined to `web/src/lib/licence-url-identity.ts` and its test, plus any report that prints the bucket. Whoever takes it should decide the enum question on its merits — I am recording the defect, not the design.

### Provenance

Reported by the #1057 QA gate (issue comment on #1057) as one non-blocking finding, correctly not held against that change. Filed separately because a finding recorded only in a gate comment on a closed issue is not work anyone will pick up.

items.title: Wire Qwen Flash + ESA hosting baseline / 接入 Qwen Flash 与 ESA 托管基线
items.body:
## Goal / 目标

Use **Qwen Flash** as Xiaohai's first real AI provider for development and early testing, using the free Alibaba Model Studio quota.

使用 **Qwen Flash** 作为小海第一阶段真实 AI Provider，优先使用阿里云百炼免费额度。先验证产品、速度和成本，再决定是否升级更强模型。

## Current infrastructure decision / 当前基础设施决定

- **Hosting:** Alibaba Cloud ESA Functions & Pages, **Global (Excluding Chinese Mainland)**.
- **Media/storage:** keep existing images/media in **Baidu BOS**.
- **AI provider:** Alibaba Model Studio / Qwen.
- **Default model:** **Qwen Flash**.
- **Future:** keep provider/model configurable so we can upgrade later without rewriting the product flow.
- **Local secrets:** developer-local `.env`, already gitignored.
- **Deployed secrets:** inject through the ESA/runtime secret/environment mechanism. Never commit real secrets.

> BOS is object/media storage only. Do not store API keys in BOS.

## Qwen configuration / Qwen 配置

Use the China OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

`https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`

Expected configuration:

```env
AI_PROVIDER=QWEN
DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=...
QWEN_BASE_URL=https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
STORY_AI_PROVIDER=QWEN
STORY_AI_MODEL=qwen-flash
```

Do not hard-code the model name inside story business logic. Read it from configuration.

## Secret handling / 密钥安全

### Local development

The real API key lives only in the developer's local `.env`.

The repo already ignores `.env`; never commit it.

Never put the key in:
- `apps/miniapp`
- WXML / frontend TypeScript
- Git
- GitHub Issues or PRs
- logs
- Baidu BOS

### Staging / production

Inject `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` into the backend/worker runtime through Alibaba ESA/runtime secret/environment configuration.

The Mini Program must call Xiaohai API, never Qwen directly.

## Runtime flow / 调用流程

```
WeChat Mini Program
        ↓
Xiaohai API
        ↓
AI Job / Provider Adapter
        ↓
Qwen Flash

Images/media
        ↓
Baidu BOS
```

## Story scope / 儿童故事范围

Start with the existing Story AI workflow:

```
idea
→ age/theme/style
→ outline
→ story
→ rewrite / continue / polish
→ save
```

Qwen Flash is the baseline model. Do **not** optimize prematurely for a stronger paid model.

Later we may escalate selected requests to a stronger Qwen model based on measured quality, latency and cost.

## Performance benchmark / 性能测试

We need real measurements for a typical **10–15 page children's book**.

Create a repeatable benchmark using the same prompt/input and record:

- total generation time
- time to first token where available
- total output tokens
- input/output token usage
- retries/timeouts
- success/failure
- story quality notes
- whether output required regeneration

Test at least **5 runs**.

Test two approaches:

1. **Single generation:** outline + complete 10–15 page story in one request.
2. **Structured generation:** outline first, then page/scene content through the Xiaohai workflow.

Report:
- p50 total latency
- slowest run
- average tokens
- failures
- which approach is simpler/faster
- any obvious quality problems

### Initial target

This is a measurement target, not a hard acceptance gate:

- text-only 10–15 page children's story should feel interactive, ideally **well under 1 minute**
- no unnecessary serial model calls
- do not generate pages one-by-one if one structured call can safely produce the same result
- image generation is a separate future benchmark and must not be included in the Qwen Flash text timing

## Acceptance / 验收

- [ ] Qwen provider adapter implemented using the existing provider architecture.
- [ ] `qwen-flash` is configurable and is the current default Story AI model.
- [ ] Real API key works from local `.env`.
- [ ] API key never reaches the Mini Program/client.
- [ ] Existing mock AI mode still works.
- [ ] One real Xiaohai Story AI request succeeds through Qwen Flash.
- [ ] Failures use Xiaohai's normal API error shape.
- [ ] Usage/error metadata is recorded without secrets.
- [ ] 5-run 10–15 page benchmark completed and results added to the PR/issue.
- [ ] Tests added/updated.
- [ ] No secrets committed.
- [ ] No unrelated infrastructure rewrite.

## 中文说明

- 托管：Alibaba Cloud ESA Functions & Pages，Global (Excluding Chinese Mainland)。
- 图片/媒体：继续使用 Baidu BOS。
- AI：阿里云百炼 Qwen。
- 第一阶段默认模型：**Qwen Flash**。
- 先使用免费额度测试，不急着升级付费模型。
- 本地 Key 只放开发者自己的 `.env`。
- 线上 Key 以后通过 ESA/runtime secrets 注入。
- 微信小程序禁止直接调用 Qwen。
- 需要真实测试生成一本 **10–15 页儿童故事** 的速度，至少跑 5 次并记录 p50、最慢一次、token 使用和失败情况。
- 图片生成后续单独测试，不要混入本次 Qwen Flash 文本性能结果。

## Git

Branch:

items.body:
## Objective

Turn the existing Hermes Core + Agent Plugin + Connector stack into one customer-installable desktop product that can run on a blank machine without requiring Python, pip, uv, Git, Node, Homebrew, Chocolatey, or other developer tooling.

Canonical execution plan:

- `docs/2026-08-07-hermes-desktop-cross-platform-execution-plan.md`
- `docs/2026-08-07-hermes-managed-runtime-customer-installation-design.md`

## Architecture baseline

```text
Hermes Desktop (Tauri 2 + Svelte)
        ↓ local IPC
Hermes Runtime Manager (Rust)
        ↓
Managed Runtime
├── Private CPython
├── pinned uv
├── Hermes Core
├── Agent Plugin
└── Connector
```

The Runtime Manager is the only lifecycle authority. Desktop UI closure or crash must not stop the Agent runtime.

Platform bootstraps:

- macOS: LaunchAgent + UDS + Keychain
- Windows: user-scoped background bootstrap + Named Pipe + Credential Manager/DPAPI
- Linux: systemd --user + UDS + Secret Service on an explicit supported-distribution matrix

Windows and Linux must remain fail-closed until their real platform adapters and blank-machine full-chain gates pass.

## P0 Shared Foundation

- [x] DESKTOP-001 create `hermes-desktop/`
- [x] DESKTOP-002 Tauri 2 + Svelte shell
- [x] DESKTOP-003 create `hermes-runtime-manager/` Rust binary/crate
- [x] DESKTOP-004 freeze Runtime Manager state machine
- [x] DESKTOP-005 freeze `ServiceManager` platform port
- [x] DESKTOP-006 freeze `SecretStore` platform port
- [x] DESKTOP-007 freeze `LocalIpc` platform port
- [x] DESKTOP-008 freeze `ProcessIdentity` platform port
- [x] DESKTOP-009 freeze `InstallLayout` platform port
- [x] DESKTOP-010 freeze manager IPC v1
- [x] DESKTOP-011 Toolchain Manifest v1
- [x] DESKTOP-012 Managed Release Manifest v1
- [x] DESKTOP-013 remove PATH `uv` dependency from customer release assembly
- [x] DESKTOP-014 private CPython toolchain
- [x] DESKTOP-015 offline wheelhouse contract
- [x] DESKTOP-016 Desktop status UI
- [x] DESKTOP-017 onboarding shell
- [x] DESKTOP-018 diagnostics shell
- [x] DESKTOP-019 tray/menu abstraction
- [ ] DESKTOP-020 blank-machine test harness
  - [x] DESKTOP-020A native zero-host-dependency qualified-toolchain gate
  - [ ] DESKTOP-020B official-installer blank-machine full-product gate
    - [ ] DESKTOP-020B1 bootstrap payload: Desktop + Runtime Manager binary + qualified Private Toolchain
    - [ ] DESKTOP-020B2 Managed Release payload: Core + Agent Plugin + Connector + offline wheelhouse
    - [ ] DESKTOP-020B3 signed installer artifacts: macOS DMG/PKG + Windows NSIS/MSI + Linux DEB
    - [ ] DESKTOP-020B4 blank-machine acceptance VM: install → login/pair → Agent Ready → Cloud → live Session → restart recovery

> Evidence note (2026-08-07): `ManagedReleaseAssembler` is now the guarded customer-runtime production composition root; it requires a SHA-verified private Python/uv toolchain plus a lock-bound verified offline wheelhouse. CI rejects production code that bypasses this path and directly instantiates the lower-level `ReleaseBuilder`.
>
> **Three-platform Desktop local read-only status transport is green in CI.** macOS and Ubuntu use UDS; Windows uses a SID-scoped Named Pipe. The native Tauri shell consumes a real Runtime Manager `Status` response on all three platforms. `Status/Doctor` are allowed; control requests remain fail-closed.
>
> macOS/Linux sockets are mode 0600 under mode-0700 state roots and additionally authenticate the OS peer user (`getpeereid` on macOS, `SO_PEERCRED` UID/PID on Linux).
>
> Windows Named Pipe has a protected current-user-only DACL at creation time, a current-user SID-scoped pipe name, remote-client rejection, client PID evidence, impersonated client-token SID comparison, bounded IPC framing, and response flush-before-disconnect. Runtime Manager and Tauri Desktop consumer tests are green.
>
> **DESKTOP-014 closure evidence:** macOS arm64, Linux x86_64, and Windows x86_64 all pass the real four-stage private toolchain gate: `Build unqualified bundle → source/license qualification → Rust Runtime Manager installs only the qualified bundle → installed provenance + Private Python/uv execution verification`. The qualification step locks uv `0.12.2` and python-build-standalone `20260805` to immutable commits/license blobs, scans runtime-carried license/notice evidence, emits `LICENSE-EVIDENCE.json`, and includes provenance files in the final per-file SHA manifest. Installed verification requires those evidence files to remain inside the immutable toolchain root and match their recorded SHA-256 values. This is engineering provenance evidence, not a claim of legal-review sufficiency.
>
> **DESKTOP-017 closure evidence:** the native Desktop now routes an incomplete install into an evidence-driven First Run shell instead of dropping the user into a falsely healthy Cockpit. The flow exposes six gates — Desktop foundation, Enterprise Cloud, Device pairing, Managed Runtime, Model service, Ready — and derives status only from the native Runtime snapshot. Missing Runtime Manager, Cloud, Connector, Core/Plugin, or provider evidence keeps the corresponding gate blocked; the shell only transitions to `RuntimeCockpit.svelte` when the full onboarding evidence predicate is satisfied. Browser mode retains an explicit design preview. Svelte static check/build and Tauri native shell checks on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows are green.
>
> **DESKTOP-019 closure evidence:** Hermes Desktop now enables Tauri 2 `tray-icon` and keeps Desktop window lifecycle separate from Runtime lifecycle. The tray menu provides Open Hermes, Hide window, and explicit Quit Hermes; left-click restores/focuses the main window where supported. Main-window close is intercepted and converted into Hide, while `ExitRequested` without an explicit exit code is prevented so the tray process can remain available after the last window is hidden. Only explicit Quit calls `app.exit(0)`. Tauri `cargo check` and the existing Desktop↔Runtime Manager native consumer tests are green on macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows. Linux always receives a tray menu, matching the current Tauri platform requirement for reliable tray visibility.
>
> **DESKTOP-020A closure evidence:** macOS arm64, Linux x86_64, and Windows x86_64 all pass a native Runtime Manager blank-machine toolchain gate under an empty/poisoned `PATH`. The gate requires `python`, `python3`, `pip`, `pip3`, `uv`, `git`, `node`, `npm`, `cargo`, and `rustc` to be unavailable from the host PATH; installs a qualified bundle into a fresh sandbox; re-verifies source/license provenance; then executes only the manifest-bound absolute Private Python/uv paths. Reports assert `host_path_isolated=true`, `provenance_verified=true`, and `private_runtime_executed=true`. Linux/macOS carry 3 locked upstream license files + 42 runtime license/notice files; Windows carries 3 + 44. Reports intentionally assert `full_product_lifecycle_verified=false`, so DESKTOP-020 remains open until the official installer VM gate proves login/pair/runtime activation/Agent Ready/Cloud/live Session without dependency-preparation steps.

## Immediate platform spikes

### Windows

- [x] WIN-SPIKE-001 Rust Runtime Manager ↔ Named Pipe ↔ Private Python test host
- [x] WIN-SPIKE-002 user SID / pipe ACL / peer PID proof
  - [x] real Named Pipe Status round-trip
  - [x] client PID proof
  - [x] same-user token SID proof
  - [x] explicit current-user DACL at pipe creation
  - [x] current-user SID-scoped stable pipe naming
  - [x] Desktop native consumer proof
- [x] WIN-SPIKE-003 Credential Manager current-user secret proof
  - [x] `CRED_TYPE_GENERIC` / `CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE`
  - [x] binary secret put/get round-trip
  - [x] overwrite round-trip
  - [x] delete + post-delete None
  - [x] idempotent delete
  - [x] target name excludes secret material and rejects unsafe key components
  - [x] generic credential blob size enforced before Win32 call
- [ ] WIN-SPIKE-004 user-logon restart/recovery proof
  - [x] WIN-SPIKE-004A native Task Scheduler current-user logon registration/run proof
  - [ ] WIN-SPIKE-004B real logoff/logon or reboot recovery acceptance

> **WIN-SPIKE-001 closure evidence:** Windows Server 2025 CI installs the source/license-qualified Hermes Private CPython `3.13.14`, poisons `PATH`, starts the real Rust Runtime Manager `serve-read-only`, and launches `private_ipc_test_host.py` with the manifest-bound Private Python executable under the Hermes toolchain root. The Python host connects through the real SID-scoped Named Pipe, receives a v1 `Status → Snapshot`, then sends `Start` and verifies it fails closed with `read_only_transport`. Report fields include `private_python_under_toolchain_root=true`, `status_snapshot_received=true`, `control_failed_closed=true`, and `verified=true`.
>
> **WIN-SPIKE-003 closure evidence:** Windows Server 2025 GitHub runner executes the real `WindowsCredentialSecretStore` against `Advapi32` Credential Manager. The Windows Runtime Manager suite ran the binary secret put/get/overwrite/delete proof and all related input/size gates with zero failures. The adapter stores only application-defined generic credential bytes in `CredentialBlob`, uses `CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE`, frees `CredReadW` buffers with `CredFree`, and never encodes secret bytes into the credential target/user name. This closes the secure-storage viability proof; restart/bootstrap remains separately tracked under WIN-SPIKE-004.
>
> **WIN-SPIKE-004A closure evidence:** Windows Server 2025 GitHub runner executes the real Task Scheduler COM integration test against the Cargo-built `hermes-runtime-manager.exe`. The adapter registers a current-user `LogonTrigger` task with `InteractiveToken`, least-privilege/LUA principal semantics, an absolute Runtime Manager executable path, `MultipleInstancesPolicy=IgnoreNew`, `StartWhenAvailable`, and `RestartOnFailure` (`PT1M`, count 3), with no password or HighestAvailable elevation. Registration identity is bound to the current token SID and COM-normalized account identity. A dedicated execution probe records `LastRunTime` before `Run`, requires a fresh `LastRunTime` after execution, waits for the registered task to leave queued/running, and requires `LastTaskResult == 0`. The integration test then deletes the task and verifies post-delete absence. The final Windows job ran 19 Runtime Manager unit tests plus 1 Task Scheduler integration test with zero failures; the integration test completed in 0.26s. This closes native registration/manual-run viability only. WIN-SPIKE-004B remains open until a persistent Windows acceptance VM proves the task is automatically invoked by a real logon/reboot and the Runtime Manager/Named Pipe recover without manual intervention.

### Linux

- [x] LINUX-SPIKE-001 Rust Runtime Manager ↔ UDS ↔ Private Python test host
- [x] LINUX-SPIKE-002 SO_PEERCRED / UID / PID proof
- [x] LINUX-SPIKE-003 systemd --user restart/recovery proof
- [x] LINUX-SPIKE-004 Secret Service proof on the first supported Ubuntu LTS target

> **LINUX-SPIKE-001 closure evidence:** Ubuntu 24.04 CI installs the source/license-qualified Hermes Private CPython `3.13.14`, poisons `PATH`, starts the real Rust Runtime Manager `serve-read-only`, and launches the Python interoperability host using the manifest-bound private interpreter. The host connects to `/home/runner/.local/share/hermes/state/rm.sock`, receives a v1 `Status → Snapshot`, then proves a `Start` request is rejected as `read_only_transport`. The JSON evidence reports `private_python_under_toolchain_root=true`, `status_snapshot_received=true`, `control_failed_closed=true`, and `verified=true`.
>
> **LINUX-SPIKE-003 closure evidence:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 CI runs the real `systemd --user` integration against the Cargo-built Runtime Manager. Hermes writes a private user unit whose only `ExecStart` is the absolute Runtime Manager `serve-read-only`; the unit uses `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=1s`, `UMask=0077`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`, and `WantedBy=default.target`, with no Python/Connector child ownership in systemd. The integration executes `daemon-reload → enable --now`, verifies `LoadState=loaded / ActiveState=active / SubState=running / MainPID>0` plus a live UDS `Status → Snapshot`, sends `SIGKILL` to MainPID, proves `Restart=on-failure` returns with a fresh PID and restored UDS, executes `systemctl --user restart` and proves another fresh PID + UDS, then disables/removes the unit. The real integration test `systemd_user_bootstrap_recovers_runtime_manager_and_uds` completed successfully in 1.64s.
>
> **LINUX-SPIKE-004 closure evidence:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 CI runs a real GNOME Keyring Secret Service session over D-Bus, not a file fallback or `secret-tool` wrapper. `LinuxSecretServiceStore` uses keyring `4.1.6` with the zbus Secret Service backend, keeps the same 2560-byte maximum as Windows Generic Credential storage, rejects unsafe namespace/account material, maps missing entries to `None`, and makes delete idempotent. The live integration test writes a binary secret containing NUL/high-bit bytes, reads exact bytes, overwrites it, reads the replacement, deletes it, verifies post-delete `None`, and deletes again successfully; `secret_service_round_trip_supports_binary_secret_overwrite_and_delete` completed successfully in 0.07s.

## Blank-machine invariant

For every platform acceptance VM:

```text
No Python
No pip
No uv
No Node
No Git
No developer tools
```

The only allowed customer-facing path is:

```text
official installer
→ open Hermes
→ login
→ pair
→ activate Managed Runtime
→ configure provider
→ real Agent Ready
→ Cloud Connected
→ live Session
```

No Terminal / PowerShell dependency-preparation steps are accepted as product closure.

## Definition of Done

This issue closes only when the shared Runtime Manager and private toolchain foundation exist, macOS can reuse them for its production closure, and Windows/Linux spikes prove that the platform abstraction is viable without introducing a second lifecycle implementation.
